raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status" },
  "read": "The mistake stung their confidence, and now every keystroke feels like a potential repeat disaster. The triple-checking is not conscientiousness — it is fear dressed up as diligence. Under that, there is a status wound: they shipped something a customer caught, which in their mind means everyone now sees them as the person who messes up. Velocity craters when someone is trying to survive rather than perform.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Reassure them that it is fine and the mistake was no big deal — which sounds kind but signals that your standards are negotiable and accidentally confirms that slowness is acceptable now." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the mistake was real, hold the delivery standard firmly, and reframe the triple-checking as a brain recalibrating after a hit — normal, temporary, and something you can work through together with a concrete system rather than raw anxiety.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Delivery pace and quality both matter — one does not get to cancel the other permanently.",
    "The customer-catch standard is a real one; the response to it needs to be a sustainable process, not paralysis."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How they build confidence back in — a checklist, a quick peer review pass, a defined sign-off step — is their call to shape.",
    "The timeline for getting back to full velocity can be graduated if they are working a real plan, not just treading water."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I want to catch up with you one-on-one — not about the ticket, just about how you are doing since it happened. That kind of thing lands hard, and I want to make sure we are actually talking about it rather than pretending it did not occur." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When you are reviewing work right now, what does that process look like for you? I am asking because I want to understand what is going on, not audit you — I just want to get a real picture of where your head is at." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I am seeing from the outside: the care you are putting in right now is real, but the way it is showing up — reviewing everything twice, three times — is not a process, it is anxiety running the show. That is a completely normal reaction after a miss, and it is also not sustainable. What if we built an actual structured check that you trust, so your brain has somewhere to land instead of just looping? I would rather spend thirty minutes building that with you than watch you burn energy on fear." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I want to be straight with you: the standard here is good work delivered at a pace that serves the team and the customer, and I am not moving off that. But I am holding you to it because I think you are fully capable of it — the mistake does not change that read for me at all. One slip does not define the arc. What I need from you is a sustainable process and a plan to get velocity back to where it was — and I think you can put that together. What does a first step look like?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Once they have a structured review process they designed and trust, start pointing out the work that lands clean — make the competence visible so their internal story shifts from 'person who made the mistake' to 'person who built a better system because of it.' That reframe is what turns a setback into a professional identity marker they carry forward."
}
situation: A junior shipped something with a mistake a customer caught, and now they are triple-checking everything and velocity has cratered.
